AISLES.name: Poetry, from scratch
AISLES.sign: Forms, sounds, and how poems get built

items.why: Every term you'll trip over, from anaphora to volta, with examples from real poems.
Short, plain explanations of forms like the sonnet, ghazal and pantoum, with poems to read alongside.
A free, open course built on close reading out loud with other people. No grades, no gatekeepers.
Thousands of recordings of poets reading their own work. Hear where the line breaks actually breathe.
The avant-garde, sound poetry and concrete poetry, collected outside the market since 1996.
Public-domain poetry collections, free to read and download in any format.
Free, carefully produced editions of public-domain poetry. Their own production work is dedicated to the public domain (CC0), so the craft is free too.
A no-login directory of free classic ebooks. The links lead out to Project Gutenberg, Apple Books and similar.

AISLES.name: Where words come from
AISLES.sign: Etymology and the history of English

items.why: Where most of the word histories on this site start. Look up any word and follow it back.
Etymologies, old spellings and cousins in other languages, for nearly every word you can think of.
The classic dictionary of Old English, searchable. See what words like rūn and spell meant first.
The language's whole story, episode by episode, from Proto-Indo-European forward.
A working etymologist untangling hard cases, including why glamour and grammar are the same word.

AISLES.name: How they sell it to you

items.why: The father of PR explaining, in his own words, how to engineer what the public wants. Read it as a confession.

items.t: State of Deception: The Power of Nazi Propaganda
items.why: How a modern state sold hatred, piece by piece, with the actual posters, films and newspapers.
Thousands of ads, industrial and educational films. Watch how the 20th century was taught to want things.
Over 7,000 U.S. and Canadian print ads from 1911 to 1955. Propaganda you can sort by year.
Free lessons on telling news from opinion, ads and misinformation.

items.by: Carl Bergstrom and Jevin West, University of Washington
items.why: A full free course on spotting nonsense dressed up in numbers, charts and big data.
A short, free book of practical moves for checking a claim online in minutes, not hours.
Stop, investigate the source, find better coverage, trace claims back to the original. One page, use it daily.
The serious version: what makes a bad argument bad, and where philosophers still disagree.
The mind's shortcuts and blind spots, each linked to the research behind it.
Sagan's checklist from The Demon-Haunted World for testing a claim before you believe it.

items.by: Rethinking Schools and Teaching for Change
items.why: Free lessons on history as working people, strikers and organizers lived it.
Marx, Engels, Trotsky, Luxemburg, Du Bois and hundreds more, free, in dozens of languages.
Short enough to read in a sitting. Read the original before you trust anybody's summary of it.
Who Built America? and other resources on the people who actually did the building.
News and how-to guides for rank-and-file organizing, written by and for workers.
Independent socialist magazine since 1949. Much of the archive is free online.
Socialist magazine with an eye for design. Most articles can be read free online.

AISLES.name: The esoteric shelf
AISLES.sign: Occult history, read with a skeptic's eye

items.why: A sourced map of the field: Hermeticism, alchemy, Rosicrucians, and how scholars study them.
Read the Hermetic texts themselves, with an introduction on where they actually came from.

items.t: European Society for the Study of Western Esotericism
items.why: The academic side: historians studying esotericism as history, not as something to sell you.
A library of hermetic, alchemical and mystical books, with digitized rare works.
Free digitized alchemy manuscripts, medical magic and the history of what people believed about the body.
Peer-reviewed and free. The best first stop for Hegel, Nietzsche, Kierkegaard, dialectics, anything.
A second opinion with clear, readable entries.
The history of philosophy told in order, for people with jobs.
Full Ivy League lecture courses, recorded and free. The classroom without the debt.
Hegel's works and study guides in one place, the root of the dialectic.
Tens of thousands of free books: Nietzsche, Dostoevsky, Marx, Emerson, and every classic past copyright.

AISLES.name: Art, collage & the public domain
AISLES.sign: Free images to study, cut and remix

items.why: Strange, beautiful public-domain finds with essays on where they came from.
Curated sets of images the Library believes are free to use, from posters to photographs.
More than 900 posters made by artists the government put to work in the Depression. Public art as public works.
Millions of images released copyright-free. Download, cut, remix, no permission needed.
Scanned magazines going back a century: ads, layouts and type to study and cut up.
Thousands of scanned pulp magazines. Lurid covers, cheap paper, and the art that came with them.
Public-domain golden-age comics, free to download.
Free art history from hundreds of scholars: essays and short videos, no textbook required.

AISLES.name: Find your voice, get it out

items.why: Grammar, structure, citing sources. The handbook everyone uses, free.
A library that takes zines seriously, with guides on making and finding them. Print it yourself.
Where to send your poems, with what each magazine publishes and how to submit.
Free public-domain audiobooks read by volunteers, and anyone can volunteer to read.
